sarah (support): FYI we've got an active customer escalation (acct: zebra-media) — spike of 5xx/429s during traffic surge. They are on Dedicated in us-west2 with min_replicas=0, max_replicas=20. Latency jumps ~3-4s then 429s. Repro steps below.

mike (eng-platform): Can you paste the request ID or sample logs? Is this the same pattern as earlier warmup/starvation cases?

sarah (support): Request IDs: r=Z12345, Z12346. From their trace: immediately after burst, probe requests queue up and get 504 from the attach service, then orchestration delays creating new pods ~10-20s. Important: they have warm_pool disabled. Logs: 
```
2026-03-16T09:12:01Z orchestrator: enqueue scale-up probe for svc/dedicated-zebra
2026-03-16T09:12:02Z attach: auth token refresh triggered, attach request delayed 1.8s
2026-03-16T09:12:04Z k8s: pod create accepted
2026-03-16T09:12:06Z registry: pull backoff (throttle) for image redwood/dedicated:stable
2026-03-16T09:12:12Z readiness-probe: timed out -> request routed to fallback -> 429s
```

anish (eng-runtime): Interesting — two signals: auth refresh delay and registry pullback. Token refresh is intermittent across some customer control planes since last rollout. Can you check attach service logs for the attach status codes?

sarah (support): attach shows repeated 401->200 for same session for a few minutes, e.g. `attach: sess=abc123 status=401 retry->200`. Also noticed the autoscaler holdoff is set to 15s for this pool. Their traffic pattern is a sudden 200 qps spike from a scheduled load test.

kevin (oncall): If min_replicas=0 and warm_pool is off, cold start path includes auth + image pull + model unpack which can be 10-25s. Combined with autoscaler conservative holdoff we see headroom misses. Could be worsened if preflight probes are serial and limited concurrency.

mike (eng-platform): Noting registry throttle — are we hitting container registry rate limits on this cluster? Which registry region? If so, that elongates pull time and then readiness deadlines hit. Also, deploy-bot shows a recent control-plane rollout 2h ago that touched token caching behavior.

sarah (support): Repro steps I used against a staging replica of their stack: 
1) Set min_replicas=0, warm_pool=false, autoscaler.holdoff=15s, max_replicas=10
2) Run `hey -z 1m -c 50 -q 0 -m POST https://dedicated-usw2.redwood/test` with burst ramp at 0s
3) Observe queued probes and 429s after spike start.

anish (eng-runtime): Can you attach the exact probe config? If readiness timeout < total coldstart path, we will never mark pod ready and the autoscaler will keep trying. Also, check preflight throttles limit in the allocator.

sarah (support): Probe snippet: `readiness: path=/health timeout=3s period=2s failureThreshold=3`. Model unpack usually takes 6-10s for this model. So probe timing is too tight for cold start.

mike (eng-platform): That matches. Two quick causes: (A) probe timeouts vs cold unpack (B) external registry throttle (C) intermittent attach auth refresh. The noisy neighbor is unlikely — CPU/GPU metrics for the node pool look normal.

kevin (oncall): Short-term mitigation for customer: bump min_replicas to 2 or enable warm_pool (recommend min_replicas=1 + warm_pool=enabled) and increase readiness timeout to 12s. Also add a small headroom buffer policy (e.g., warm_headroom=15%).

sarah (support): I proposed: 1) temporary min_replicas=1 and readiness timeout 12s; 2) ops to check registry quota and if needed switch to a cached image mirror; 3) eng-runtime to review attach token caching rollback. Customer accepted the temp plan.

anish (eng-runtime): I'll look into attach token caching. If token refresh is serialized per cluster and we hit a race during heavy attach bursts we can add a short jitter and local token cache TTL bump. I'll open a rollback candidate for the control-plane config and run a canary in us-west2.

mike (eng-platform): I'll check registry metrics and talk to registry provider about pull throttling and propose a mirrored cache in us-west. Also will add a quick autoscaler heuristic override that temporarily relaxes holdoff when preflight failure rate climbs.

sarah (support): For the support ticket I added repro commands, suggested config changes, and scheduled a 2pm PST follow-up after we test the warm_pool change.

deploy-bot: [notice] control-plane rollout started by anish at 2026-03-16T10:32:00Z

kevin (oncall): Planned follow-ups: (1) apply customer temp config and validate in 10m (sarah), (2) eng-runtime to revert or fix token caching if repro confirmed (anish), (3) eng-platform to report registry rate/solutions (mike). If we don't see improvement within 30m escalate to SEs.

sarah (support): Update at +12m after applying min_replicas=1 & readiness=12s: customer traffic steady, no 429s observed, tail latency down to ~220ms. They reported a single 503 during immediate switchover. They are good with the mitigation while infra teams investigate root cause.

anish (eng-runtime): Root cause summary candidate: combination of tight readiness probe timings and serialized attach token refresh backed by a thin token cache introduced in the last control-plane rollout. Fix options: bump local cache TTL and add jitter; increase probe defaults for zero-warm nodes; or make warm_pool default true for dedicated customers with min_replicas=0.

mike (eng-platform): Filing follow-up RFC for: - autoscaler emergency holdoff relaxation heuristic - warm_pool opt-in for sudden-burst customers - registry mirror guidance in onboarding docs.

sarah (support): Closing customer ticket as mitigated; leaving this thread open for infra follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: [incident] ticket#8921 marked mitigated by sarah at 2026-03-16T10:46:09Z

kevin (oncall): Thanks all. If anyone finds additional surprises in the attach logs ping here.
